income-tax-calculator.assumptionNote: Uses the 2025 US federal single-filer brackets and the 2025 standard deduction ($15,750). State taxes, credits, and capital gains are not included. Brackets change yearly - verify the current table before filing.
benefits: Get a quick federal tax estimate before you file - no tax software needed.
See your marginal vs effective rate: the number that matters for raises and bonuses.
Test how a bigger deduction or extra income changes your tax.
Free, instant, and private - no personal details leave your browser.

faqs.a: No. The US uses marginal brackets: only the income inside each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate. So moving into the 22% bracket taxes only your dollars above $48,475 at 22% - everything below is still taxed at 10% and 12%.
faqs.q: Does moving into a higher bracket tax all my income?

faqs.a: The marginal rate is the tax on your next dollar of income (22% in the worked example). The effective rate is total tax divided by total income (13.45% here). The marginal rate drives decisions about raises and bonuses; the effective rate describes your overall burden.
faqs.q: Marginal vs effective tax rate - what is the difference?

faqs.a: For 2025 it is $15,750 for single filers. It is the amount subtracted from income before tax applies. If your itemized deductions (mortgage interest, charity, state taxes) exceed it, you itemize instead.
Long-term capital gains have their own lower rates (0%, 15%, 20%) and are not included here. Neither are Social Security or Medicare taxes, which add about 7.65% on wages for the employee.
faqs.q: Does this include capital gains or payroll taxes?

faqs.a: State income tax is completely separate and varies from 0% (Texas, Florida) to over 13% (California). This calculator covers federal tax only, so your real total is higher in most states.
Brackets are inflation-adjusted every year. This calculator uses the 2025 table. If you are filing for 2026 or later, check the IRS for the current year's brackets before relying on the result.

income-tax-calculator.formula:
Taxable income = gross income - deduction
Tax = sum over brackets of (income in bracket x bracket rate)
2025 single brackets: 10% to $11,925; 12% to $48,475; 22% to $103,350;
24% to $197,300; 32% to $250,525; 35% to $626,350; 37% above.
Effective rate = total tax / gross income x 100.
howTo: Enter your deduction - the 2025 single standard deduction of $15,750 is pre-filled.
Read your estimated federal tax, taxable income, marginal rate, and effective rate.
Adjust income or deduction to compare scenarios.
keyFacts: The US federal income tax is progressive: higher income is taxed at higher marginal rates.
Only income inside each bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate.
The 2025 standard deduction for single filers is $15,750.
State tax, credits, and capital gains are separate and not included here.
